newsitem.title: THAILAND: IFCT agrees Bkk Bank of Commerce takeover terms.
newsitem.headline: IFCT agrees Bkk Bank of Commerce takeover terms.

text.p: The semi-government Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand on Friday said its board had agreed on terms to takeover management of ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.

The IFCT board had agreed to a proposal to buy 18.5 percent of the bank's shares from the central bank's rehabilitation fund at 10 baht per share, costing a total of 6.57 billion baht, IFCT said in a statement filed to the Thai stock exchange.
IFCT agreed to consider running the bank after a bidding process for the takeover of the bank fell through at the end of last year.

BBC shares have been trading in high volumes since coming off an 11 month suspension last week. The stock was up 0.50 baht to 6.20 baht by the lunchbreak on Friday and was the most actively traded counter.
Traders say IFCT and existing BBC shareholders might have been buying shares in order to bring down the average cost of their stakes.
IFCT has agreed to pay the Rehabilitation Fund for its 18.5 percent holding in installments, the statement said.
The first installment amounts to five percent of the total share purchase, or 329 million baht.

IFCT has an option to sell back its stake in BBC to the Rehabilitation Fund at par value plus interest on the payment made for shares at a rate 250 basis points below the Minimum Lending Rate per year, the statement said.
